page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 2 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing a total of 2 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is rated as weak, while multi-core performance falls into the bottom 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write speeds measured at 12.97 GB/sec and 11.91 GB/sec respectively. Passmark CPU and memory scores confirm this positioning, with a CPU score of 2138.85 and a memory score of 1418.01.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but modest resource footprint, the ecs.c6e.large offers a cost-effective entry point for lightweight compute tasks. It is suitable for basic web serving, simple microservices, and low-traffic database operations where dedicated CPU resources are preferred over shared-core burstable instances. However, it is not suited for memory-intensive applications, high-throughput data processing, or parallelized workloads.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-based instance delivers modest performance, with benchmarks indicating weak single-core and poor multi-core capabilities. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with large-block read speeds of 12.97 GB/sec. Qualitatively, the ecs.c6e.large represents a budget-friendly option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without high memory demands. It is best suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving, and small-scale microservices.
